metadata.description: Curated collection of Claude Code plugins for modern full-stack development with LLM performance tracking and E2E skill testing

plugins.name: code-analysis
plugins.description: Extracted mnemex + claudish MCP servers into dedicated runtime plugins (declared via dependencies)

plugins.name: claudish
plugins.description: Claudish MCP runtime — external model proxy with team voting, async sessions, and channel notifications. Required by code-analysis, dev, multimodel, designer, agentdev, seo. Dual-published to magus and magus-marketing because seo depends on it.

plugins.name: mnemex
plugins.description: Mnemex MCP runtime — semantic code search and AST analysis with PageRank. Required by code-analysis and dev.

plugins.name: multimodel
plugins.description: Declared claudish as a dependency (extracted into a dedicated runtime plugin)

plugins.name: agentdev
plugins.description: Declared claudish as a dependency (extracted into a dedicated runtime plugin)

plugins.name: dev
plugins.description: Dropped the conductor-missing coaching rule — the conductor plugin is retired, so the suggestion pointed at commands that no longer ship. The /dev:design-system command validates any project against the design-system guardrails: token-only styling, one component library, variants over call-site restyling.

plugins.name: go
plugins.description: Go development toolkit. Ships the go-tui skill for building colorful, graph-and-badge-heavy terminal UIs with the Charm stack (Bubble Tea, Lip Gloss, Bubbles, ntcharts), plus a verified color-accurate screenshot workflow (tmux capture → aha → headless Chrome → PNG) so you can see and critique a running TUI in full color.

plugins.name: dingo
plugins.description: BETA — Dingo language skills: idiomatic Result/Option types, error propagation (?), enums, pattern matching, lambdas, and safe navigation, with compiler-verified patterns. Interfaces may still change.

plugins.name: statusline
plugins.description: Adaptive statusline — always-visible bars, background highlights for critical states, provider-aware model display, vim mode, diff stats, compaction count, memory usage. v2.1.2: Split diff section into session (✨ +A/-D from Claude Code cost telemetry) and git (● +A/-D from `git diff --shortstat`) chips, so users can tell the difference instead of seeing stale session totals on a clean worktree.

plugins.name: browser-use
plugins.description: Full-platform browser automation for Claude Code. Live-page JS eval, keyboard/focus primitives, and env preflight; configurable agent LLM (Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible/Browser Use BU3); dual local/cloud browsers, orphaned-Chrome reaping, and Playwright's bundled Chromium so your real Chrome is never hijacked. 26 MCP tools, 6 skills.

plugins.name: designer
plugins.description: Declared claudish as a dependency (extracted into a dedicated runtime plugin)

plugins.name: terminal
plugins.description: Pane-occupancy safety: PreToolUse:Bash hook (bun/TS) blocks raw tmux send-keys/kill-pane/split-window into non-shell panes (sibling claude sessions, REPLs); skills document the foreground-check rule and split-pane idle-reuse (reused:true) contract

plugins.name: gtd
plugins.description: GTD (Getting Things Done) workflow integration. v2.0.0: Canonical GTD terminology (Clarify, Engage), sequential task IDs (#1, #2), boxed terminal display, reference list, Bun display tool. Real-time sync via hooks, 7 commands, 2 skills.

plugins.name: kanban
plugins.description: Kanban board view for task management. v1.6.0 (breaking): Kanban decouples from GTD — independent store at .claude/kanban/tasks.json with a kanban-only schema (status field, no GTD overlay). Legacy tasks in .claude/gtd/tasks.json are NOT auto-migrated; re-add via /kanban:add. Visual board with 5 columns, task dependencies (cycle-safe), priority indicators, WIP limits.

plugins.name: madbench
plugins.description: Toolkit for madbench, MadAppGang's Go harness for benchmarking agentic coding tools. Ships the madbench-evals skill: author bench YAML, design checks, scaffold red-state testdata, run/validate benches, tune expectations, debug failing checks.
